title: Quick check: Next.js Rendering Overview

questions.prompt: In the context of “Next.js Rendering Overview” and “Client-side rendering”, Next.js is best described as
options: a programming language that replaces JavaScript.
a database engine for storing application records.
a CSS preprocessor that only compiles stylesheets.
a React framework that adds routing, rendering choices, and full-stack conventions.
questions.answer_key: a React framework that adds routing, rendering choices, and full-stack conventions.
questions.explanation: Next.js builds on React and provides application conventions and server capabilities; it does not replace JavaScript or serve as a database.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Next.js Rendering Overview”, Which comparison is accurate for this part of the curriculum?
options: React and Next.js are both database products.
React is a UI library; Next.js is a framework that organizes a complete web application around React.
Next.js can only render static HTML and cannot support interactive UI.
A Vite-based React app and a Next.js app always have identical server features.
questions.answer_key: React is a UI library; Next.js is a framework that organizes a complete web application around React.
questions.explanation: React supplies the component model; Next.js supplies additional routing, rendering, and server-side application conventions.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Next.js Rendering Overview”, When deciding whether to use Next.js for a project, what should guide the decision?
options: Choose it solely because every React project must use it.
Assume framework conventions remove the need for testing.
Pick the framework before understanding rendering and deployment constraints.
Match the framework capabilities and operational trade-offs to the application requirements.
questions.answer_key: Match the framework capabilities and operational trade-offs to the application requirements.
questions.explanation: The supplied curriculum emphasizes benefits as well as rendering, deployment, and complexity trade-offs.
